summary: AE + SE demo of Redwood hosted embeddings and rerank endpoints. Customer is evaluating options for improving search relevance; primary concerns are latency, cost, and data control. Demo included live embedding generation, similarity search examples, and a reranking pipeline using Redwood's hosted API. Security questions (SOC 2, SSO, KMS) were raised; Redwood team to share security docs. Agreed next steps: send pricing/benchmarks, share code snippets, and kickoff POC next week.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-11 16:00 PDT | Duration 47 min | Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Kenji Ito (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (AcuitySearch Head of Search), Liam O'Connor (Sr ML Eng), Priya Rao (ENG Manager)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood Inference, I'm the AE on this account, and with me is Kenji and Jordan from our SE team. How's everyone doing?

[00:08] Maya: Hi, thanks Sofia, all good. We are excited to see the embeddings and rerank flow — we've been testing a few things in-house and want to understand how Redwood fits.

[00:18] Sofia: Awesome, quick agenda — 15 minute product walkthrough of the hosted API (embeddings + rerank), then a short search relevance walkthrough with your sample queries, and Q&A on security and pricing. Sound good?

[00:30] Liam: Yep, that works. We have about 45 mins. We're mainly worried about tail latency — sub 200ms ideally for query path, cost per 1M queries, and how you handle PII.

[00:42] Kenji: Great, we'll keep that in mind. Quick qual question — what's your current stack for retrieval? Are you using Elastic or a vector DB?

[00:52] Maya: We're on Elastic for doc store + a custom vector index in house. We also prototyped with Pinecone last quarter but ran into cost unpredictability.

[01:05] Kenji: Got it. For the demo I'm going to show our embeddings endpoint first — it's a simple POST, returns a 1536 dim vector by default for the model we use. Then I'll show how we plug that into a nearest-neighbor stage and then call our rerank endpoint to compute final relevance scores.

[01:20] Jordan: Note — hosted has auto-scaling and prefix caching options; if you need tighter latency and isolation we can talk dedicated later.

[01:30] [02:05] Kenji: Switching to the screen here. Okay, terminal first — hitting /v1/embeddings with a small batch of queries. Response comes back in ~120-150ms for this model on our hosted tier, your results may vary by region and model. Apologies if the screen share blips a bit.

[02:30] Liam: 120-150ms from request to embedding? That's pretty good. What's the tokenization overhead?

[02:40] Kenji: For short queries it's small — under 10ms usually. The bulk is model inference. We also do streaming for generation endpoints but for embeddings it's a single response.

[03:00] Maya: How are you storing embeddings? We want to avoid sending raw user PII off-platform.

[03:08] Sofia: For hosted we have redaction guidance and support customer-side PII hashing before sending. Also Redwood Private / VPC option lets you keep data in your VPC with a customer-managed control plane if that's required.

[03:25] Liam: Ah okay — need to confirm whether PII-in-transit is allowed for our compliance. We'll need SOC2 docs and details on KMS.

[03:34] Sofia: Absolutely, we'll share SOC 2 report, security overview, and KMS integration notes after the call.

[03:42] [05:10] Kenji: Next step, nearest neighbor lookup — here I show a quick similarity search against a small index. Using cosine similarity on the embeddings, top-k returns are shown. You can tune distance metric, index type, and use Faiss or external vector DBs (Pinecone, Weaviate) — Redwood doesn't force you into our index.

[05:40] Maya: Good. Our current recall is okay but precision drops on long-tail queries, that's where we want a reranker.

[05:52] Kenji: Right — so then we call the /v1/rerank endpoint. You send the query + candidate docs (either text snippets or ids with embeddings) and the model returns a relevance score. We support batching so you can include hundreds of candidates in a single API call, and we return normalized scores.

[06:15] Jordan: Small note — continuous batching in our runtime groups requests to improve throughput, there's also KV cache for prefix reuse; sometimes in transcripts it's misheard as KV cash but it's cache.

[06:28] Liam: Heh, good to know. What's typical latency for rerank on, say, 10 candidates?

[06:36] Kenji: For a 10-candidate rerank on hosted, you're looking ~80-120ms additional. Combined with embedding + NN lookup network hop it can hit ~220-280ms — depends where your vector DB is hosted. If you colocate in same region it tightens up.

[06:58] Maya: So to keep sub-200ms we'd need to optimize NN lookup locality and maybe reduce candidate size?

[07:06] Kenji: Exactly, options: 1) reduce candidate pool with better recall upstream, 2) push NN into same VPC/region, or 3) use a cheaper, faster model for embeddings and a stronger model for rerank — Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching configs to hit cost/latency targets.

[07:28] Maya: Is Redwood Optimize part of hosted or an add-on?

[07:32] Sofia: It's an add-on/toolkit that sits in the Console — gives recommendations on batching, quantization profiles, model choices per workload. We'll include a sample Optimize report in the benchmark sheet.

[07:45] [09:00] Kenji: Live example — I send a user query "best noise cancelling headphones under $200". Embedding step, NN returns top 50 docs, then rerank sorts top 10 by relevance. You'll see the reranker surface product-specific signals and reorder results compared to raw embedding score.

[09:20] Priya: The reorder looks promising. How deterministic is the reranker? We need consistent ranking for A/B tests.

[09:30] Kenji: Rerank is deterministic given same inputs and model version. You can pin model versions in the deployment config and do canary rollouts. Also we provide trace ids so you can re-run scoring for audit.

[09:45] Liam: What about model drift monitoring? We need alerts if relevance drops after a model update.

[09:53] Jordan: Console has quality monitoring tied to prompt sets/eval sets; you can set regression alerts based on your test queries. We'll show a sample dashboard in the POC. Sometimes names are garbled in transcripts like 'quality moni-tor' but the feature is there.

[10:10] Maya: Regarding security — does hosted store logs? How long do you retain requests? We need to meet a 90 day retention or shorter based on policy.

[10:20] Sofia: Hosted stores request logs by default for 30 days for debugging; retention can be adjusted and extended at enterprise tiers. For strict retention you can use Private deployment and control logs in your environment. All logs are encrypted at rest, and we support customer KMS for dedicated/private.

[10:40] Liam: Any RBAC / SSO support?

[10:44] Sofia: Yes, Console supports SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC roles, and audit logs. We'll include the SSO integration guide.

[11:00] [13:15] Kenji: Back to performance — here's a microbenchmark I ran earlier: embedding call 130ms median, rerank 95ms median for 10 candidates, 99th percentile for rerank around 250ms on hosted. Dedicated GPU pools reduce the long tail.

[13:32] Maya: Sounds reasonable. Can we control model choice? We need to try a smaller embedding model for speed.

[13:40] Kenji: Absolutely; the hosted catalog exposes multiple model variants. You can pick a smaller embedding model for fast retrieval and a larger reranker for final scoring. Redwood's routing can fall back to cheaper model variants if capacity is constrained.

[13:55] Liam: What's the pricing model — per embedding + per token for rerank? How do you price batch calls?

[14:05] Sofia: Hosted is usage-based: per-embedding vector unit and per-token for generation/rerank (depending on model). Batch calls are charged per item processed. We'll send a benchmark sheet that lays out sample cost calculations for your query volumes.

[14:24] Priya: We typically do ~1.2M queries/month, average 25 candidate reranks per query — cost calc will be important.

[14:34] Sofia: We'll model that in the spreadsheet and show a hosted vs dedicated cost projection.

[14:50] [20:00] Kenji: Quick note on integration patterns: 1) client side -> embeddings call -> store vectors in your existing vector DB -> nearest neighbor -> call rerank with top-k; 2) or use Redwood-managed index (we can host vectors) if you prefer less infra. Both are supported.

[20:25] Maya: If we host vectors ourselves, can rerank accept doc ids instead of full text? We want to avoid sending full doc body.

[20:33] Kenji: Yes, rerank accepts ids + precomputed embeddings so you can keep documents in your DB. If you send ids Redwood will fetch embeddings from the payload. We also support hashed ids and recommend PII hashing for sensitive fields.

[20:50] Liam: Are there SDKs for the rerank flow or only REST?

[20:55] Jordan: We have SDKs for Python, JS, and a small Golang client. We'll share the code snippet in the follow up.

[21:10] Maya: Any limitations on candidate set size? We occasionally need 200-300 candidates for reprocessing in experiments.

[21:18] Kenji: Hosted rerank supports large batches but latency grows linearly. For very large candidate sets we recommend preliminary filtering (embedding nearest neighbors) then rerank the top subset. For experiments we can also run offline batch reranks.

[21:40] [28:00] Sofia: Ok, let's go over compliance. Maya, Liam — you asked about SOC2, KMS, VPC. We'll send SOC2 and HIPAA guidance if needed; our Private deployment offers a customer control plane and on-prem option. For hosted we support customer-managed KMS in dedicated tiers.

[28:28] Maya: Good. For our procurement team we'll need an outline of SLAs, data residency, and the contract template.

[28:36] Sofia: I'll include SLA summary and a sample MSA. For procurement I'd expect an initial pilot on hosted, then evaluate dedicated/reserved if we need capacity guarantees.

[28:50] Liam: Timeline — we're planning a Q2 pilot. If POC looks good we want an accelerated rollout by end of Q2.

[28:58] Sofia: That fits. Suggested next step: POC kickoff 3/18, we'll scope acceptance criteria (latency target, relevance metrics), and run a 2-week pilot.

[29:10] [33:00] Kenji: Quick demo wrap — showing a simple A/B example, we push two rerank model versions and compare NDCG on a held-out set. Console tracks the evals and flags regressions.

[33:30] Maya: That dashboard looks useful. Do you keep model change audit logs?

[33:36] Jordan: Yes, we keep model versioning and rollout history in the Console. You can pin versions per route.

[33:50] Priya: One question on rate limiting — we have spikes during launches; how do you handle burst capacity?

[33:58] Sofia: Hosted has soft quotas and rate limits; for spikes we have burst capacity and Dedicated supports guaranteed throughput. We'll include burst policies in the doc.

[34:12] Liam: Any comments on open-source alternatives? We tested Weaviate but it's been operationally heavy.

[34:20] Sofia: Customers often combine a vector DB like Weaviate/Elastic with Redwood for scoring. Redwood focuses on inference and routing so you avoid building the model serving stack yourself.

[34:35] [41:00] Kenji: Final quick items — sample code we'll share includes: embedding + NN + rerank pipeline, a small benchmark harness, and Optimize recommendations. Also a post-demo security FAQ.

[41:20] Maya: Great. Can you share the code snippets and the benchmark with costs by 3/12?

[41:28] Sofia: Yes — Sofia will send pricing + benchmark by 3/12, Kenji will send code + tuning notes by 3/13, and we'll schedule POC kickoff for 3/18.

[41:45] Priya: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.

[41:50] Sofia: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials and calendar invite.

[42:00] End of recording.
notes: Customer prioritized latency <200ms end-to-end, precision on long-tail queries, and strict data residency/PII controls
Recommended architecture: embeddings hosted + customer vector DB colocated in same region + Redwood rerank hosted; alternative: Redwood-managed vector index for simpler infra
Agreed POC: 2-week pilot, kickoff 2026-03-18, success metrics include NDCG improvement >10% and median query latency <220ms
